2. Facts relevant for the disposal of the above rule may briefly be stated as follows : 

 The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 304 of 1973 against the opposite party Nos. 2-4 as defendant Nos. 1 to 3 and opposite party No. 5 as proforma defendant No. 4 for a declaration that the lands described in the plaint-schedule are appartmant to the plaintiffs Waqf Estate and that no Compensation Assessment Roll or retention of choice-list with regard to the Waqf Estate has been prepared or published in terms of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and fules there under and that the plaintiff is entitled to continua in his possession and with the maintenance and management of the Waqf Estate described in the plaint schedule and for permanent injunction restraining the main defendant Nos. 1-3 from interfering with the plaintiffs possession, maintenance and management of the Waqf Estate. 

 11. Mr. JN Deb, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner nextly submits that the judgment and order dated 19.4.78 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge refusing plaintiff's prayer for temporary injunction against the opposite party No. 1 in respect of SAS plot No. 1638 was quite reviewable in as much as as there was error apparent on the face of the same and also for other sufficient reasons. Elaborating his argument the learned Advocate submits that from a bare reading of the impugned judgment and order dated 19.4.78 it would be found that although the application for temporary injunction by the plaintiff was against defendant No. 5/opposite party No. 1 only in respect of a solitary plot namely SAS plot No. 1638, the learned Subordinate Judge has taken into consideration the case of other defendants and their written statement against whom there was already an order of temporary injunction before adding opposite party No. 1 as a defendant which was made absolute as far back on 7.5.74 and who did not challenge the said order of temporary injunction in any higher forum. Of course, in the ultimate consideration of the case of the defendant No. 5 along with that of the other defendants, the learned Subordinate Judge came to a finding the the plaintiff petitioner failed to make out a prima-facie arguable case for injunction and observed that an order of status-quo be better maintained, but while passing the order dated 19.4.78 he rejected the prayer of the plaintiff/petitioner for temporary injunction against the defendant No. 5/opposite party No. 1 in respect of SAS plot No. 1836 and vacated the ad-interim order passed earlier. Mr. Deb further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge has also committed illegality in taking into consideration the question of maintinability of the suit on the alleged ground of non-service of prior notice under section 94 of the Basic Democracies Order 1959 while deciding the application for temporary injunction. In this connection he has referred to some decisions one in the case of Dacca Match Factory Ltd Vs. Bangladesh Match Co. Ltd reported in 30 DLR (HC) page 244 para 8 wherein it has been observed by a Division Bench of this Court.
